coverage: Deterministic, bounded, versioned world-seed system plans with unique names and stable resource identities.
The star chart and resolved orbital scenes exist at startup before any navigation menu is opened.
All regions in a system share the same celestial body identities, sizes, colors, seeds and relative geometry.
All twelve new regions have independent surface dimensions, matching atmosphere and surface-sky body identity.
Reload preserves the saved chart, selected generated destinations, edited scenes and existing home scene.
Controller, local/long-range scanners, advanced navigation and station population use the owning server chart.
Native sessions reject forged routes while accepting the expanded server catalog; legacy terminal pagination uses server-supplied identities.
Graphical journey: original planets, generated outer planet, actual landing, surface sky, relaunch to its orbit, moon jump and return to Terra.
Automatic stations continue populating generated orbital regions.
All native guide pages fit the book height and content asset checks include the generated dimensions in the test preset.
qualification: An initial complete run was deliberately stopped after finding the isolated flat-world preset lacked the twelve new dimension entries. The preset and asset validation were updated.

The next run found an old five-route assertion and an overflowing guide page. The assertion now checks the saved server catalog; star-system guidance has its own short chapter. Guide and navigation passed in isolation and in this full run.

Generation adds a bounded four-system chart with static allocated surface identities. The landable terrain reuses existing rocky, ocean and moon flat-world templates; unlimited galaxy generation and procedural biome terrain are outside this pass.
